title: Playbook: Phaseout of batch/webhook export adapters and migration to streaming-export API
creator: Ivy Chen
background: We currently support two legacy export surfaces used by customers for bulk ingestion: the batch export HTTP webhook adapter and the bulk-export file bundle endpoints. Both paths predate the streaming-export API and have diverging semantics (batched retries, per-file manifest state, ad-hoc backfill behavior). Maintaining these adapters increases operational complexity, causes inconsistent user experience for delivery guarantees, and blocks improvements to at-least-once streaming semantics and structured progress events.
goals: 1) Provide a clear migration path for customers from batch/webhook and bulk-export to the streaming-export API. 2) Remove the two legacy adapters with a coordinated timeline and safety gates. 3) Ensure data fidelity and delivery guarantees match or exceed legacy behavior. 4) Ship SDK helpers, migration docs, and a compatibility gateway for customers requiring additional runway.
non_goals: We will not redesign customer data schemas during migration. We will not force on-prem or private tenants to upgrade underlying on-prem agents prior to the compatibility window but will require security sign-off for any bridge components.
scope: In-scope: phased removal of batch webhook adapter and bulk-export endpoints, compatibility gateway (6 month TTL), streaming-export SDK helpers, documentation, telemetry gates, and rollback procedures. Out-of-scope: rearchitecting downstream consumer storage, changing export payload schemas, and on-prem agent replacement (handled by separate Private infra project).
migration_steps: 1) Publish migration guide and SDK helpers (JS, Python, Go) with code samples for converting batch semantics to streaming-export with idempotency keys and resume tokens. 2) Offer an optional compatibility gateway (hosted) that accepts legacy calls and emits streaming-export events; document guarantees and rate limits. 3) Run a shadowing program (opt-in customers) to mirror legacy exports to streaming-export for parity validation. 4) Provide a migration CLI that validates manifests and suggests mapping rules for per-file metadata. 5) Coordinate customer outreach for high-impact accounts with SEs. 6) Toggle deprecation flags and begin phased shutdown windows with 60/30/14/7-day notices. 7) Final cutover and 30-day post-shutdown support window.
rollout_timeline: - Week 0 (now): Announce deprecation and publish migration guide. - Week 4: SDKs and migration CLI v1 released. - Week 8–12: Offer compatibility gateway, start opt-in shadowing. - Week 16: Begin enforced soft-deprecation (telemetry-backed rate limits on legacy adapters). - Week 24: Hard-shutdown of batch webhook adapter with 30-day open support. - Week 32: Hard-shutdown of bulk-export endpoints. Exact dates will be pinned once telemetry gates are met.
acceptance_criteria: 1) SDK helpers published and examples convert 95% of internal sample manifests without manual intervention. 2) Shadowing parity: for at least 90% of mirrored exports, delivery order and payload checksum match between legacy and streaming-export during a 4-week shadow period. 3) No high-severity data loss incidents attributable to migration in shadowing customers. 4) Telemetry gates: error rate for streaming-export <= 1.5x legacy adapter baseline and 95th percentile end-to-end latency within agreed SLO for migrated traffic. 5) Customer adoption: >= 60% of active export users have migrated or are on compatibility gateway prior to hard-shutdown phase. 6) Runbook and rollback verified by SRE and security review completed.
telemetry_gates: We will track: migration adoption rate by customer and endpoint, parity checksums between legacy and streaming export, per-customer error rate delta, 95th/99th latency percentiles, compatibility gateway error/queue depth, and SDK download/adoption metrics. Gate thresholds will be set in coordination with SRE (ENG-4218).
rollback_plan: Compatibility gateway remains online throughout the shutdown window and can be re-enabled to accept legacy traffic if parity failures exceed threshold. Hard-shutdown steps include: 1) Pause client-facing shutdown and re-open legacy ingress for impacted customers. 2) Roll back rate limit enforcement flags. 3) Re-run shadowing and triage with engineering on root cause. 4) Communicate extended timeline to affected customers and execs.
stakeholders: PM: Ivy Chen; Eng owners: Marcus Lee (api-ingest), Priya Nair (streaming-runtime); SRE: Carlos Mendes; Docs/DE: Hannah Ortiz; Legal & Security: Rahul Kapoor; Solutions Eng: Jamie Park; Sales: Olivia Turner; Support: Melissa Wong.
docs_and_client_guidance: Contents to publish: migration overview, decision matrix (compatibility gateway vs direct migration), code recipes for JS/Python/Go, CLI mapping tool, FAQ, customer-facing timelines and SLAs for the compatibility bridge, and sample manifests for common edge cases (multipart files, retries, idempotency). All docs will be published to Confluence + public developer portal and cross-linked from the Console migration banner.
operational_playbook: SRE runbooks for partial failures, high queue depth on compatibility gateway, and data replays. Include contact chain, runbook steps, how to trigger manual replay, and post-mortem template. Define escalation: Pager for production parity regressions, Slack channel #export-migration, bi-weekly migration sync.
customer_communication: Initial announcement email + in-console banner with migration checklist. Tiered follow-ups: 60/30/14/7 days before shutdown to all impacted accounts. Targeted SE outreach for top 20 customers. Provide migration office hours and a dedicated support queue. Templates for support engineers and account execs included.
security_and_compliance: Compatibility gateway will pass through existing authentication (API keys and token-based) and honor per-customer rate limits and retention policies. Security review (formal) required and tracked under ENG-4490. Any data-at-rest created by gateway will follow KMS policies and be ephemeral where possible.
related_artifacts: - Migration guide draft (Confluence link placeholder) - SDK PRs: github.com/redwood/sdk-js/pulls/1234, sdk-py/pulls/567 - ENG-4218 parity evaluation doc - Compatibility gateway architecture diagram (Drive link placeholder) - Support runbook draft
notes: We will prioritize low-latency customers for direct migration support. For customers on private deployments, coordinate with the Private infra team to determine compatibility bridge hosting requirements. Track all customer exceptions as scoped tickets and include in final post-shutdown audit.
follow_up_tasks: 1) Schedule security review (owner Rahul Kapoor). 2) Finalize SDKs and publish npm/pypi packages. 3) Build in-console migration banner experiment. 4) Create migration CLI release pipeline and E2E test harness. 5) Book migration office hours calendar.
